title: Responses protocol adapter: stable fragment reassembly, toolcall boundaries, and seed handoff for OpenAI compatibility
author: Marissa Cole
release_notes: Compatibility adapter: stable streaming reassembly across Responses variants, explicit tool/function-call boundary markers, and passthrough of RNG/seed hints to Redwood sampling for deterministic debug runs. No API breaking changes.
description: Motivation: New OpenAI Responses variants expose streaming fragmentation semantics, RNG/seed hints, and richer metadata that must be faithfully represented in Redwood's Responses compatibility layer. Without an adapter, hosted customers see reordering and truncated toolcall boundaries in streamed responses and cannot reproduce outputs when a seed is provided. This PR implements a protocol adapter that stabilizes fragment reassembly, preserves explicit tool/function-call boundary markers in the stream, and forwards RNG/seed hints plus metadata passthrough to the sampling layer. Design highlights: 1) Introduce lightweight fragment framing (frag_id, seq, final_flag) on the bridge to detect out-of-order chunks and perform deterministic reassembly with minimal buffering. 2) Emit and consume explicit toolcall boundary tokens at the adapter layer so function/tool callers receive well-formed call begin/end events even when the underlying runtime shards streams. 3) Map OpenAI-style "seed"/"deterministic" hint fields to an internal RNG-hint header and expose a seed proxy that pins sampling when requested for reproducible debug runs. 4) Preserve response-level metadata (request_id, model_attrs, user_metadata) by passthrough on the adapter and tag primary streaming frames with metadata headers so the console and observability pipelines retain attribution. 5) Fail-open fallback: when fragment integrity cannot be verified within a configurable timeout, the adapter falls back to per-chunk best-effort delivery and flags the event in logs/metrics. Implementation notes: Changes are concentrated in services/bridge/openai_adapter.go (adapter logic and framing), runtime/stream/framer.go (framing helpers), runtime/stream/reassembly.go (reassembly state machine), runtime/sampling/seed_proxy.go (seed handoff and validation), api/compat/responses_adapter_test.go (unit/integration tests), and docs/compat/openai-responses.md (compatibility guide). The adapter is feature-flagged under "openai_responses_adapter_v2" and gated behind a canary rollout. Tests and validation: added deterministic integration tests that replay recorded fragment orders, end-to-end tests against an OpenAI-compat harness, and a small perf canary to verify latency impact under 99th-percentile SLOs. Observability: new metrics added: adapter.frag_reassembly.latency_ms, adapter.frag_reassembly.reorders, adapter.toolcall.boundary_mismatches, and adapter.seed_forward.count. Rollout plan: 1) enable on internal canary; 2) run for 48h comparing toolcall event counts and reassembly metrics; 3) enable on hosted region eu-west-1 with gradual traffic ramp; 4) flip feature flag for Dedicated customers based on contracts. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] canary config, [x] docs updated, [x] rollout plan added. Impact: backward compatible for existing calls, minor latency increase in worst-case reassembly situations, improves streaming stability and deterministic reproduction for debugging. Related: ENG-3241 tracks the adapter work; SUP-9123 references a customer case where streamed toolcalls were split across fragments.
commits_summary: 7 commits: initial adapter scaffold and feature flag; framing helpers and proto changes; reassembly state machine with tests; seed proxy + sampling integration; toolcall boundary markers and console tagging; docs and compatibility guide; canary config and CI pipeline adjustments.
review_comments: Eliot Wong: Looks solid overall. Two asks: (1) tighten the reassembly buffer cap and expose as config; (2) add a small fuzz test that randomly reorders fragments to validate the state machine. Also please add a short migration note for Dedicated customers.

Marissa Cole (author): Addressed buffer cap and exposed via adapter.max_reassembly_buffer; added fuzz test suite under api/compat/fuzz_reassembly_test.go; added dedicated migration note in docs. PTAL.

Diego Alvarez: Approve after the perf numbers are posted from the canary run. Concern: seed passthrough must never override customer KMS restrictions; ensure validation rejects externally-supplied seeds if KMS-policy forbids it.
Marissa Cole (author): Added validation gate in runtime/sampling/seed_proxy.go that checks customer seed policy via authz call; updated tests to cover the restricted case.
Samir Patel: Left a nit on log level for boundary-mismatch (info -> warn) and a small comment about metric cardinality. Resolved by adjusting to warn only when mismatch rate > threshold.
merge_summary: Squash and merge. Merge commit message: 'openai(compat): responses protocol adapter with stable fragment reassembly, toolcall boundaries, and seed handoff. Closes ENG-3241.'
